claims.text: An integrated data-driven machine-learning framework can concurrently optimize phase stability, microstructure refinement, and mechanical or functional properties in multiphase metallic systems.
The target material initially has a coarse, multiphase microstructure containing unstable phases.
A machine-learning method can use experimental and simulation data to determine optimal strain-rate, temperature, and time parameters.
Molecular-dynamics and Monte Carlo results are suitable inputs to the proposed processing-optimization framework.
The proposed treatment combines severe plastic deformation with controlled thermomechanical processing under parameters selected by machine learning.
The optimized processing will produce a nano- or ultrafine refined microstructure.
The optimized microstructure will contain stabilized coherent precipitates and phase boundaries, such as coherent delta lamellae and embedded secondary phases.
Coherent precipitates and phase boundaries act as barriers to microstructural coarsening.
Integrating multiscale experimental and simulation data into a machine-learning model identifies processing conditions that promote a controlled phase-transformation pathway.
The machine-learning-selected phase-transformation pathway simultaneously suppresses coarsening, refines the microstructure, and stabilizes desired phases.
Tailoring alloy microstructures can improve material properties.
The refined and phase-stabilized microstructure will improve mechanical or functional properties.
Compared with conventional thermomechanical treatments, machine-learning-optimized processing will enhance phase stability.
Compared with conventional thermomechanical treatments, machine-learning-optimized processing will produce significant microstructure refinement.
Compared with conventional thermomechanical treatments, machine-learning-optimized processing will improve strength, ductility, or other functional properties.
Traditional thermomechanical or single-step processing generally improves either microstructure or phase stability individually rather than in an integrated manner.
The effectiveness of the approach depends on the range and quality of the machine-learning training data.
Complex phase-transformation kinetics may limit the approach in some alloy systems.
Early studies and simulation trends support the optimization of complex processing parameters using data-driven models.
The interplay between severe deformation and phase stabilization under machine-learning-selected conditions has not yet been rigorously validated.
